title: CNN Foundations: Inductive Biases, Receptive Fields & Spatial Math
raw_content:
[00:00 - 05:00] Good morning. Today we cover Convolutional Neural Networks. Standard MLPs fail on high-resolution images because flattening a 256x256 image creates 200,000 parameters and erases spatial locality.
[05:00 - 15:00] CNNs introduce two vital inductive biases: local connectivity and weight sharing. This guarantees translation equivariance: shifting the input shifts the feature map identically.
[15:00 - 32:00] Pay close attention to this derivation: O = floor((W - K + 2P)/S) + 1. Worked example: W=32, K=5, P=2, S=1 -> O = floor((32 - 5 + 4)/1) + 1 = 32. If S=2 and P=0, O = floor((32 - 5)/2) + 1 = 14.
[32:00 - 50:00] Receptive field stacking: three 3x3 layers cover a 7x7 receptive field with 27C^2 parameters instead of 49C^2 for a single 7x7 filter, while providing 3 non-linearities.
[50:00 - 60:00] In summary: local receptive fields, parameter efficiency, and translation equivariance form the cornerstone of visual representations.
